resource.name: North Star Metric Finder
resource.description: Four-step wizard returns three candidate North Star metrics with arguments for and against, vanity-risk analysis, leading-vs-lagging, gameability, and an input-metric tree per candidate.

tools.name: nsm_candidates
tools.description: LLM-narrated. Generates three candidate NSMs given structured wizard inputs.

tools.name: nsm_dashboard_audit
tools.description: LLM-narrated. For each metric in the user's pasted dashboard, labels it closest-to-NSM, useful-input, or vanity-replace, with a one-line reason.

tools.name: nsm_calibration
tools.description: MCP-only (stateful). Compares the user's chosen NSM against where it sits now. Has it moved? Has it surfaced the failure mode it was supposed to surface? Stores prior NSM picks + values locally across runs.

_meta.dev.workingfromlenny.phase_note: Web version does not expose this tool. Calibration requires persisted prior picks + current value in the .mcpb bundle's data dir; host's confirmation UI handles the consent surface.

_meta.dev.workingfromlenny.comment: MCP resource spec for #9 North Star Metric Finder. Phase 2 .mcpb bundle target. Validated against MCP Apps spec (Jan 2026 release + current draft) on 2026-05-18.
dev.workingfromlenny.open_questions: Should the input_metrics tree share a schema with #37 Activation Metric Finder so the two apps interoperate, or stay independent?
Dashboard audit: how to handle dashboards >40 metrics gracefully? Truncate with a 'audit the top 40' notice, or batch?
Calibration tool: who provides the current_nsm_value — pulled from a connected analytics tool, or user-entered? Latter is .mcpb-scope by default.
dev.workingfromlenny.proposed_answers: Stay independent for Phase 2. The .mcpb format has no inter-bundle schema import mechanism; bundles are self-contained. Schema alignment between #9 and #37 is worth revisiting when both apps are production-ready and usage patterns are clear. For now the input_metrics array of strings is fit for purpose. Note this as a Phase 3 consideration for #37 spec work.

Truncate with a notice. 'I will audit the first 40; paste a second batch for the rest' is the right UX. Batching requires the host to sequence calls and merge results, which adds client-side complexity. The 40-metric cap is also a soft forcing function: if a team has 80 dashboard metrics, the real insight may be 'this is too many metrics to have' before the audit even runs. A one-line notice makes that implicit point.

User-entered for Phase 2. Pulling from a connected analytics tool requires a data-source integration that is out of scope. User entry of the current NSM value is sufficient for the calibration pattern. Flag the analytics integration as a Phase 3 consideration, same rationale as the mortality tool on #24 OKR Critique.

notes: ui:// scheme is valid; no rigid format is enforced — server-defined slugs after the scheme are acceptable.

No requires-consent / data-retention / fs-write capability exists in either ext-apps appCapabilities or .mcpb manifest. Consent is host-discretion; readOnlyHint: false on stateful tools is the only normative hook.
Underscore-prefixed fields at non-_meta paths have undefined host behavior; project metadata lives under _meta with reverse-DNS keys.
